title: post api auth register user registration
description: Test POST /api/auth/register with a unique email and valid password. Expect 201 Created and a top-level user payload containing id and email, with no token payload. Duplicate registration should return HTTP 400; the API may return either field-level validation keys such as email or an error wrapper, so do not require a specific error envelope.

title: post api auth login user authentication
description: Test POST /api/auth/login after creating a user. Expect 200 OK with an access token in the JSON body and the refresh token set only as an HttpOnly cookie, not in the JSON body. Invalid credentials should return 401.

title: post api auth logout invalidate session
description: Test POST /api/auth/logout with a valid Bearer access token after login. The refresh token should come from the login cookie. Expect 204 No Content and verify the refresh cookie is cleared. A later refresh attempt without the cookie may return 400 for a malformed refresh request or 401 for an unauthorized refresh.

title: post api auth refresh token refresh
description: Test POST /api/auth/refresh after login. The current contract reads the refresh token from the HttpOnly refresh_token cookie and returns only a JSON access token. Missing refresh cookie may return 400; invalid refresh cookie should return 401.

title: get api auth me get authenticated user profile
description: Test GET /api/auth/me with a valid Bearer access token from login. Expect 200 OK with a top-level user payload including email and id. A request without authorization should return 401.

title: get api auth sso provider get sso metadata
description: Test GET /api/auth/sso/provider with an authenticated default-organization owner or admin user. Expect 200 OK and a top-level payload containing status. When no provider is configured, status.state should be unavailable. Unauthenticated requests should return 401.

title: post api graphs validate graph payload validation
description: Test POST /api/graphs/validate with Bearer auth. The payload shape is { graph_json: {...}, strict?: boolean }. Use this valid graph_json exactly for positive cases: {"nodes":[{"id":"output-1","type":"output","name":"Output","config":{}}],"edges":[{"id":"edge-1","from":"START","to":"output-1"}]}. Responses are wrapped under data. A valid graph returns 200 with data.valid=true. A semantically invalid but structurally well-formed graph can return 200 with data.valid=false and errors. Missing graph_json returns 400.

title: post api graphs create new workflow graph
description: Test POST /api/graphs/ with Bearer auth. This endpoint creates graph metadata only, not graph versions, so send { name, description? }. Expect 201 Created and a data wrapper containing id, name, version_count=0, and latest_version=null. Missing name should return 400.

title: post api runs start start graph run
description: Test POST /api/runs/start with Bearer auth. First create graph metadata using POST /api/graphs/ with {name, description?}, then create a graph version via POST /api/graphs/{graph_id}/versions using this valid graph_json exactly: {"nodes":[{"id":"output-1","type":"output","name":"Output","config":{}}],"edges":[{"id":"edge-1","from":"START","to":"output-1"}]}. Do not use node types start/end because they are not valid runtime node types. Start the run with { graph_version_id, input_json? }. Expect 201 Created with a data wrapper containing id, graph_version_id, status, and input_json. A nonexistent graph_version_id should return 404.

title: post api runs engine events receive engine callback
description: Test POST /api/runs/engine-events as a server-to-server callback, not as a user-authenticated endpoint. The current callback auth headers are X-ForgeGraph-Timestamp and X-ForgeGraph-Signature, not X-Engine-Signature. Signatures are HMAC-SHA256 over `${timestamp}.` plus the exact raw body, where timestamp is milliseconds since epoch. Do not hardcode a shared secret in generated tests. If ENGINE_CALLBACK_SECRET is not available to the test process, only assert that invalid and missing signatures return 401. If ENGINE_CALLBACK_SECRET is available, create a real run first, send a valid body containing type, run_id, tenant_id, event_id, and timestamp, then expect 200 and duplicate=true on repeat.
